title: Potential and Kinetic Energy
seo_title: Grade 7 Natural Sciences: Potential and Kinetic Energy Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 7 Natural Sciences: Sources of energy; potential and kinetic energy
standard_text: Energy sources are renewable (solar, wind, hydro) or non-renewable (coal, oil, gas, nuclear fuel). Energy can be stored as potential energy and is kinetic energy when objects move; mechanical energy is conserved when no energy is lost. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 7, Energy and Change: Sources of energy; potential and kinetic energy)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): renewable and non-renewable energy sources, potential energy, kinetic energy and energy conversions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Stored energy is potential energy; moving energy is kinetic energy.
key_sub: Energy changes form but is not lost.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy sources can be non-renewable (coal, oil, natural gas, nuclear fuel) or renewable (solar, wind, hydroelectric). Most of South Africa's electricity is made from coal, but solar and wind farms are growing.

Potential energy is stored energy: a raised object has gravitational potential energy, a stretched spring has elastic potential energy, food and fuel have chemical potential energy. A moving object has kinetic energy. When a ball falls, potential energy changes into kinetic energy; when it bounces up, kinetic energy changes back.

Example

A rock sits at the top of a cliff. Which energy does it have?

Stored because of its height

Answer: gravitational potential energy

Example

What energy change happens when a ball rolls down a slope?

It gets lower and faster.

Answer: potential to kinetic

Common mistakes

  • Thinking energy is used up.
  • Thinking only moving things have energy.
  • Thinking solar energy is non-renewable.

faq.a: Some energy is changed into heat and sound.
It took millions of years to form and cannot be replaced.

items.q: Why is energy never really 'used up'?
c: It changes from one form to another.
items.e: Energy is conserved.

items.q: Lindiwe asks how copper and gold ores formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries
from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
from rain and snowmelt soaking into porous rock and sediment (aquifers)
items.e: Copper and gold ores formed from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries.

items.q: Liam reads about a resource that formed from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how oil and natural gas formed.

items.q: Daniel asks how oil and natural gas formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers
from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries
items.e: Oil and natural gas formed from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years.

items.q: People use petrol in cars to get energy from oil. Which is a benefit of this energy source?
c: It stores a lot of energy in a small amount.
It is replaced naturally in a few days.
items.e: It stores a lot of energy in a small amount.

items.q: Which is used to turn sunlight into electricity or motion?
items.e: Energy from sunlight is used with solar panels.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?
items.e: Heat from inside Earth (geothermal) is renewed by nature and does not run out. Coal, oil and gas take millions of years to form.

items.q: People use a gas stove or gas power station to get energy from natural gas. Which is a benefit of this energy source?
c: It is replaced naturally in a few days.
It can make electricity day and night.
items.e: It can make electricity day and night.

items.q: Chloe asks how rock salt formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers
from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries
from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
items.e: Rock salt formed from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago.

items.q: Which energy source is not renewable?
items.e: Natural gas formed over millions of years and will run out; burning it also pollutes the air.

items.q: Which is used to turn oil (as petrol) into electricity or motion?
c: a gas stove or gas power station
items.e: Energy from oil is used with petrol in cars.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?
items.e: Sunlight is renewed by nature and does not run out. Coal, oil and gas take millions of years to form.

items.q: Elna reads about a resource that formed from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how rock salt formed.

items.q: What does 'reduce, reuse, recycle' help save?
c: resources and the energy needed to make new things
items.e: Making new products uses energy.

items.q: People use a geothermal power station to get energy from heat inside Earth. Which is a problem with this energy source?
c: It only works in places with hot rock near the surface.
Burning petrol pollutes the air, and oil spills harm ocean life.
Panels need a lot of land or roof space, and they only work when the sun shines.
Burning coal pollutes the air, and mining it damages land.
items.e: It only works in places with hot rock near the surface.

items.q: Which energy source is not renewable?
items.e: Coal formed over millions of years and will run out; burning it also pollutes the air.

items.q: People use a dam with a power station to get energy from moving water. Which is a problem with this energy source?
c: Burning petrol pollutes the air, and oil spills harm ocean life.
Burning gas pollutes the air, and drilling can harm land and water.
A dam floods land and blocks fish from swimming up the river.
Burning coal pollutes the air, and mining it damages land.
items.e: A dam floods land and blocks fish from swimming up the river.

items.q: Palesa reads about a resource that formed from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how copper and gold ores formed.

items.q: A stretched elastic band stores which form of energy?
items.e: It is released when let go.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?
items.e: Wind is renewed by nature and does not run out. Coal, oil and gas take millions of years to form.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in a plate of chicken rice?
items.e: A plate of chicken rice has chemical potential energy.

items.q: Is tidal energy a renewable or a non-renewable energy source?
c: neither, because it is not a source of energy
items.e: Tides are caused by the Moon every day.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in a charged handphone battery?
items.e: A charged handphone battery has chemical potential energy.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in a moving bus?
items.e: A moving bus has kinetic energy.

items.q: Is geothermal energy a renewable or a non-renewable energy source?
c: neither, because it is not a source of energy
items.e: Heat from inside the Earth will last a very long time.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in an electric fan?
c: chemical potential energy → kinetic energy and thermal energy
gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy
electrical energy → kinetic energy and sound energy
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of an electric fan.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in an electric kettle?
c: kinetic energy of the wind → electrical energy
gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy
chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy and thermal energy
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of an electric kettle.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in a hydroelectric power station?
c: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy
electrical energy → thermal energy, kinetic energy and sound energy
chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy and thermal energy
chemical potential energy → kinetic energy and thermal energy
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of a hydroelectric power station.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in a compressed spring?
items.e: A compressed spring has elastic potential energy.

items.q: Is solar energy a renewable or a non-renewable energy source?
c: neither, because it is not a source of energy
items.e: It will not run out, but it depends on sunlight.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in a catapult firing a stone?
c: chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy and thermal energy
kinetic energy → thermal energy and sound energy
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of a catapult firing a stone.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in a car battery?
items.e: A car battery has chemical potential energy.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in a ringing school bell?
items.e: A ringing school bell has sound energy.

items.q: Is coal a renewable or a non-renewable energy source?
c: neither, because it is not a source of energy
items.e: It is a fossil fuel.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in a diver standing on a high board?
items.e: A diver standing on a high board has gravitational potential energy.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in a person running?
c: chemical potential energy → kinetic energy and thermal energy
kinetic energy → thermal energy and sound energy
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of a person running.

items.q: What is the main form of energy in a hot iron?
items.e: A hot iron has thermal energy.

items.q: Is wind energy a renewable or a non-renewable energy source?
c: neither, because it is not a source of energy
items.e: Wind is replaced naturally.

items.q: Is hydroelectric energy a renewable or a non-renewable energy source?
c: neither, because it is not a source of energy
items.e: The water cycle replaces the water.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in a hairdryer?
c: electrical energy → thermal energy, kinetic energy and sound energy
chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy and thermal energy
chemical potential energy → kinetic energy and thermal energy
kinetic energy → thermal energy and sound energy
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of a hairdryer.

items.q: Priya observes a go-kart with 600 J of kinetic energy. If its mass is tripled but its speed stays the same, what is its new kinetic energy?
items.e: KE is proportional to mass: 3 × 600 J = 1 800 J.

items.q: Using Chloe's graph, what would the kinetic energy of the 6 kg trolley at 8 m/s be?
items.e: Double the speed of 4 m/s → 4 times the KE.

items.q: Elna observes a sledge with 200 J of kinetic energy. If its speed is tripled and its mass stays the same, what is its new kinetic energy?
items.e: KE depends on speed squared: 3² = 9, so 9 × 200 J = 1 800 J.

items.q: A ball dropped with 120 J of potential energy bounces back up with 60 J. Where did the rest of the energy go?
c: It became new mass in the ball.
It was stored in the ground forever as potential energy.
It was converted to thermal and sound energy.
items.e: Energy is not destroyed: 60 J is converted to thermal and sound energy.

items.q: A ball is dropped. What happens to its energy as it falls?
c: Gravitational potential energy is transformed into kinetic energy.
Kinetic energy turns into potential energy.
items.e: It speeds up as it falls.

items.q: A ball has 100 J of gravitational potential energy at the top of a fall. Ignoring air resistance, how much kinetic energy does it have just before it hits the ground?
items.e: Energy is conserved: all the potential energy becomes kinetic energy.

items.q: What is the law of conservation of energy?
c: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or transformed.
Energy is used up when things move.
items.e: Wasted energy spreads into the surroundings.

items.q: A ball has 20 J of gravitational potential energy at the top of a fall. Ignoring air resistance, how much kinetic energy does it have just before it hits the ground?
items.e: Energy is conserved: all the potential energy becomes kinetic energy.

items.q: A light bulb receives 60 J of electrical energy and gives out 20 J of light energy. How much energy is converted to thermal energy?
items.e: Total energy out = total energy in: 60 − 20 = 40 J.

items.q: A ball has 200 J of gravitational potential energy at the top of a fall. Ignoring air resistance, how much kinetic energy does it have just before it hits the ground?
items.e: Energy is conserved: all the potential energy becomes kinetic energy.

items.q: What does the principle of conservation of energy state?
c: Energy is created in power stations.
Energy is used up when we use it.
Energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be converted from one form to another.
items.e: The total energy stays the same.

items.q: Which formula gives work done?
c: work done = force × distance moved in the direction of the force

items.q: When is work done?
c: when an object is held still
when a force moves an object in the direction of the force
items.e: No movement in the direction of the force means no work done.

items.q: What energy transformation happens at the Snowy Hydro power stations?
c: gravitational potential energy of water → kinetic energy → electrical energy
items.e: Falling water spins turbines.

items.q: Where does a bouncing ball's 'lost' energy go?
c: It stays in the ball forever.
It is transferred to the surroundings as heat and sound.
items.e: Energy is conserved but dissipated.

items.q: A light bulb receives 120 J of electrical energy and gives out 10 J of light energy. How much energy is converted to thermal energy?
items.e: Total energy out = total energy in: 120 − 10 = 110 J.

items.q: A light bulb receives 50 J of electrical energy and gives out 20 J of light energy. How much energy is converted to thermal energy?
items.e: Total energy out = total energy in: 50 − 20 = 30 J.

items.q: What is the SI unit of energy?
items.e: Work done is also measured in joules.

items.q: A learner holds a 20 N bag still for 5 minutes. How much work is done on the bag?
items.e: The bag does not move, so no work is done on it.

items.q: A car's speed doubles. What happens to its kinetic energy?
c: It becomes four times as big.
items.e: Kinetic energy depends on speed squared.

items.q: Why is a light globe never 100% efficient?
c: Some electrical energy is transferred as heat, not light.
items.e: Useful output is always less than input.

items.q: What is the main energy change when a pendulum swings from its highest point to its lowest point?
items.e: At the lowest point it moves fastest.

items.q: A light bulb receives 200 J of electrical energy and gives out 40 J of light energy. How much energy is converted to thermal energy?
items.e: Total energy out = total energy in: 200 − 40 = 160 J.
